name: Campaign 3
description: A Bayesian state estimator has twice failed to outperform rolling trend extrapolation for early warning on SIMOC, and the standing objection was that neither benchmark gave it anything to work with: a smooth monotone single-channel ramp under a constant control input is the best case for extrapolation, and it withholds the information a model-based method exists to exploit. This campaign removes that objection. A commanded scrubber duty cycle makes the observable non-monotone. The commanded schedule is supplied to the estimator as a known control input. The fault is silent, existing only as a discrepancy between commanded operation and realised response. A masking confounder lets the raw trace flatten or fall while capacity is failing. A schedule-aware linear baseline receives the same schedule, and the estimator runs at its validated configuration. The estimator lost on every axis, by the widest margins in this series, and it alerts on healthy habitats more often than any trend method. Supplying the known control input made it worse rather than better, and it did worst on the masked case designed to be its strongest ground. Extra information helps a model-based estimator only where the model is right about how that information acts.
